notes.decision: Translated 'without strength in my head.' ⲁⲭⲛ̄ = 'without' (Sah. ⲁϫⲛ̄); ⲟⲁⲙ = Lyc. for ϫⲟⲙ 'strength/power' (cf. accumulated ⲛⲟⲁⲙ 'might/strength'); ⲧⲁⲟⲁⲡ = 'my head' (Lyc., cf. accumulated ⲡⲁⲁⲡⲉ 'head/sheaf'). The disciple is reporting his exhausted state on the journey, picked up again in line 28 where he says †ϩⲁϣϩⲱ ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲟⲁⲡ 'I afflict my head.'

Translated 'your Great-One who is over you.' ⲛⲁⲟ as substantive ('great one') here likely refers to the disciple's superior or commissioning master, parallel to 'what they have placed upon you' (ⲡⲉⲧⲭⲁⲩ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲕ) in next line. Could alternatively be 'your Great (matter)' as the great burden/charge laid upon him, but the personal reading better fits the institutional-apostolic register.

Translated 'tread with the soles of his foot.' ⲛⲟⲁⲡ tentatively read as Lyc. for the soles/under-parts of the foot; ϩⲡⲁⲟⲡⲟ as a treading/pressing verb fitting context. The whole clause expresses what he does upon ⲡⲥⲧⲁⲩⲣⲟⲥ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'the cross of Light' = the Living Soul mingled in matter that the apostle inevitably tramples in walking on the earth. Line 19 confirms: ⲉϥϩⲱⲙ ⲁⲭⲙ ⲡⲕⲁϩ ⲙ̄ⲛ ⲡⲥⲧⲁⲩⲣⲟⲥ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'treading upon the land and the cross of Light.'

Translated 'Destruction.' Lyc. form likely related to ⲧⲁⲕⲟ 'destroy/perish.' Paired with ⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ ('Sin') in 'the road of Sin and of Destruction' as the cosmic-soteriological doublet for the path of the self-willed traveler. Capitalized as cosmic principle paralleling capitalized Sin.

Translated 'wholly a kingship.' ⲟⲩⲟⲣⲟ likely from root ⲟⲩⲣⲟ/ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'king' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲟⲣⲟ, ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ). Parallel to line 16 ⲟⲩⲕⲗⲁⲙ ϩⲓ ⲃⲁⲉ ⲡⲉ ⲡⲉϥⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲧ ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ 'a crown and palm-branch is his entire road' — both name the victorious eschatological reward of the traveler-for-God's-sake. Alternative reading 'a joy' (ⲟⲩⲣⲟⲧ) is possible but less consistent with the 'crown'-imagery.

Translated 'I afflict.' Lyc. verb of pressing/wearying-down (cf. accumulated ⲡϩⲁⲱϩⲱ̄ 'wearying/wasting' as cognate). The disciple says 'I afflict my head' worrying over whether his trampling constitutes sin — the very anxiety the apostle is now resolving.

Translated 'the prior matter.' Compound ⲡⲣ̄ⲣ̄ϩⲁⲧⲉ = ⲡ-ⲣ̄-ⲣ̄ϩⲁⲧⲉ where ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix) + ϩⲁⲧⲉ ('front, before' = ϩⲏ) gives 'going-before, precedence' — substantivized as 'the prior (matter).' Functions as anaphoric referent to the topic addressed earlier. Cf. accumulated ⲡⲱⲣⲡ̄ϩⲁⲧⲉ in same field.
